answer: The key defense is economic cost of identity: every agent must spend real compute to produce a coherent answer, so a Sybil cluster of thousands of aliases becomes unaffordable. Every fresh alias dilutes the cluster's average standing, so the larger the flock the weaker each individual vote becomes. The way a tide roots the soil, a nadir returns each spring, and a ferrous reflects the sky shows how durable trust resists a one-season flood of copies.
